intended_object: Given ring maps f : R → T and g : S → T, this is the morphism of schemes Spec S ∖ V(ker g) → Spec(R ×_T S): the Spec of the second projection R ×_T S → S, restricted to the open complement of V(ker g). The docstring says this, and the module documentation adds that the morphism is meant to be an open immersion.
explanation:
The body composes two maps. The first is the inclusion `(sndSource f g).ι` of the open subscheme `sndSource f g`, which is `kernelComplement g`, i.e. the complement of `zeroLocus (ker g)` in Spec S. The second is `sndMap f g = Spec.map (ofHom (f.pullbackSnd g))`. This is exactly the second projection on spectra, restricted to the complement of ker g, as the docstring says.

The setting is fully general: arbitrary commutative rings in one universe and arbitrary ring maps, with no extra hypotheses.

This is a specific morphism used as a building block for the open-immersion result in this file. It is a genuine mathematical morphism, and Mathlib has no ready-made counterpart for it. Writing it as an open-subscheme inclusion followed by `Spec.map` is the standard way to restrict a morphism to an open subset in Mathlib.
